correctness.rationale: Completing the squared Euclidean cost inequalities gives the complement of n open disks of radius r=lambda R/(lambda²-1) with centers C=lambda²R/(lambda²-1) on the same regular ring. For each ray the nearest center angular offset |delta|<=pi/n determines the entire excluded interval; if r>C sin(pi/n), positive continuous roots rho_± split inner and outer regions with a uniform gap. At tangency the retained common tangent points join them; beyond tangency the disk interiors are disjoint and the complement path-connected with n holes. The inner radius integrates exactly to n[C² s h+r²(beta-arcsin(lambda s)-lambda s sqrt(1-lambda²s²))]. The remaining arccos(z)-z sqrt(1-z²) equals (2/3)(1-z²)^(3/2)+O((1-z²)^(5/2)), proving the stated cusp. Independent SciPy radial quadratures matched the closed area in four (n,R,lambda) choices, including n=4 square critical area 8-2pi. All bounds and tie convention verified.

value.rationale: The bounded island disappears as an isolated component at a natural disk-contact topology transition, but its area approaches a positive limit with a nonanalytic 3/2 correction. Quantified exact geometry is meaningful beyond known general disconnected weighted Voronoi cells: complete connectivity phase, closed area and cusp coefficient for every n.

final_claim: For a central site and n>=3 equally spaced competitor sites at radius R with distance lambda||x-v_j||, the central whole-plane multiplicatively weighted Voronoi cell consists of two components for 1<lambda<csc(pi/n) and one connected component for lambda>=csc(pi/n); for lambda>threshold it has n bounded holes. The subcritical bounded island has the stated elementary radial area formula and an explicit positive (threshold-lambda)^(3/2) cusp.
limitations: Whole-plane closed central cell, competitor-weight convention multiplies distance; the unbounded component has infinite area; the island-area quantity is a subcritical bounded component only.
